title: Is Planet Labs an Undervalued Space Stock to Buy Right Now in October? | PL Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Planet Labs' ~50% six-month slide is a buying opportunity. He likes the business: it turned cash-flow positive ($68M operating cash flow YTD, $21M free cash flow even after capex), holds ~$865M in cash after prudently raising ~$120M at ~$32 during the SpaceX-IPO space-stock frenzy (shares now $17.50), and remaining performance obligations grew ~9% to $753M with Q2 revenue pulled forward. Wall Street expects revenue growth of 47%/30%/28% over the next three fiscal years, and demand is shifting toward premium AI-enhanced analytics, not just imagery. But valuation kills it: his DCF fair value is $5.50 vs $17.50 market, so despite the improving fundamentals he would need roughly a 50% drop to ~$8 before buying. Call: PL AVOID at $17.50 (first tracked call on the name). Captions are garbled in spots but the numbers come through clearly.

calls.thesis: Likes the business — FCF positive, ~$865M cash, RPOs up ~9% — but his DCF fair value is $5.50 vs $17.50 market. Would need roughly a 50% drop to ~$8 before meaningfully considering a buy. First tracked Parkevtate call on PL.
calls.bull_case: Revenue re-acceleration plus AI-enhanced imagery services could drive premium margins and justify a higher multiple.
calls.bear_case: Post-SpaceX-IPO euphoria has already faded; high forward P/S of ~11 can compress further on any contract slowdown.
